avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate bleeding risk and interfere with EGFR inhibition efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E supplementation; discuss with oncology team before use

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce P-glycoprotein affecting monoclonal antibody disposition and immune response
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; use alternative herbal supplements if needed

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase bleeding tendency; cetuximab can cause skin toxicity with anticoagulant effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased bruising or bleeding; coordinate with oncology if used

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance immune response; potential to alter cetuximab efficacy unpredictably
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution and inform oncology team of concurrent use

avoid_foods.name: High-dose herbal teas (echinacea, goldenseal)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Immunostimulating effects may counteract EGFR-targeted therapy and increase infusion reactions
avoid_foods.action: Avoid herbal immune-boosting preparations during cetuximab treatment

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: While cetuximab is not CYP3A4-metabolized, grapefruit may enhance EGFR pathway effects unpredictably
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; monitor for increased skin toxicity or gastrointestinal effects

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay gastric emptying and reduce tolerability of concurrent oral chemotherapy agents
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent, moderate-fat diet; separate from cetuximab infusions by 2+ hours if possible

monitoring_notes: Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody not metabolized hepatically; interactions are primarily immune-mediated or related to concurrent therapies. Monitor closely for acneiform rash, infusion reactions, and gastrointestinal toxicity, which may be exacerbated by immune-stimulating supplements or anticoagulants.
